43:36.ar: وَمَن يَعۡشُ عَن ذِكۡرِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ نُقَيِّضۡ لَهُۥ شَيۡطَٰنࣰ ا فَهُوَ لَهُۥ قَرِينࣱ‏
43:36.en: And he whose sight is dim to the remembrance of the Beneficent, We assign unto him a devil who becometh his comrade

43:37.ar: وَإِنَّهُمۡ لَيَصُدُّونَهُمۡ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَيَحۡسَبُونَ أَنَّهُم مُّهۡتَدُونَ
43:37.en: And lo! they surely turn them from the way of Allah, and yet they deem that they are rightly guided

43:38.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَنَا قَالَ يَٰلَيۡتَ بَيۡنِي وَبَيۡنَكَ بُعۡدَ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقَيۡنِ فَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡقَرِينُ
43:38.en: Till, when he cometh unto Us, he saith (unto his comrade): Ah, would that between me and thee there were the distance of the two horizons - an evil comrade

43:39.ar: وَلَن يَنفَعَكُمُ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ إِذ ظَّلَمۡتُمۡ أَنَّكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡعَذَابِ مُشۡتَرِكُونَ
43:39.en: And it profiteth you not this day, because ye did wrong, that ye will be sharers in the doom

43:40.ar: أَفَأَنتَ تُسۡمِعُ ٱلصُّمَّ أَوۡ تَهۡدِي ٱلۡعُمۡيَ وَمَن كَانَ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
43:40.en: Canst thou (Muhammad) make the deaf to hear, or canst thou guide the blind or him who is in error manifest

43:41.ar: فَإِمَّا نَذۡهَبَنَّ بِكَ فَإِنَّا مِنۡهُم مُّنتَقِمُونَ
43:41.en: And if We take thee away, We surely shall take vengeance on them

43:42.ar: أَوۡ نُرِيَنَّكَ ٱلَّذِي وَعَدۡنَٰهُمۡ فَإِنَّا عَلَيۡهِم مُّقۡتَدِرُونَ
43:42.en: Or (if) We show thee that wherewith We threaten them; for lo! We have complete command of them

43:43.ar: فَٱسۡتَمۡسِكۡ بِٱلَّذِيٓ أُوحِيَ إِلَيۡكَۖ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطࣲ مُّسۡتَقِيمࣲ‏
43:43.en: So hold thou fast to that which is inspired in thee. Lo! thou art on a right path

43:44.ar: وَإِنَّهُۥ لَذِكۡرࣱ لَّكَ وَلِقَوۡمِكَۖ وَسَوۡفَ تُسۡـَٔلُونَ
43:44.en: And lo! it is in truth a Reminder for thee and for thy folk; and ye will be questioned

43:45.ar: وَسۡـَٔلۡ مَنۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مِن قَبۡلِكَ مِن رُّسُلِنَآ أَجَعَلۡنَا مِن دُونِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ ءَالِهَةࣰ يُعۡبَدُونَ
43:45.en: And ask those of Our messengers whom We sent before thee: Did We ever appoint gods to be worshipped beside the Beneficent

43:22.ar: بَلۡ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا وَجَدۡنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا عَلَىٰٓ أُمَّةࣲ وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِهِم مُّهۡتَدُونَ
43:22.en: Nay, for they say only: Lo! we found our fathers following a religion, and we are guided by their footprints

43:23.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ مَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مِن قَبۡلِكَ فِي قَرۡيَةࣲ مِّن نَّذِيرٍ إِلَّا قَالَ مُتۡرَفُوهَآ إِنَّا وَجَدۡنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا عَلَىٰٓ أُمَّةࣲ وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِهِم مُّقۡتَدُونَ
43:23.en: And even so We sent not a warner before thee (Muhammad) into any township but its luxurious ones said: Lo! we found our fathers following a religion, and we are following their footprints

43:24.ar: ۞قَٰلَ أَوَلَوۡ جِئۡتُكُم بِأَهۡدَىٰ مِمَّا وَجَدتُّمۡ عَلَيۡهِ ءَابَآءَكُمۡۖ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا بِمَآ أُرۡسِلۡتُم بِهِۦ كَٰفِرُونَ
43:24.en: (And the warner) said: What! Even though I bring you better guidance than that ye found your fathers following? They answered: Lo! in what ye bring we are disbelievers

43:25.ar: فَٱنتَقَمۡنَا مِنۡهُمۡۖ فَٱنظُرۡ كَيۡفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلۡمُكَذِّبِينَ
43:25.en: So We requited them. Then see the nature of the consequence for the rejecters

43:26.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوۡمِهِۦٓ إِنَّنِي بَرَآءࣱ مِّمَّا تَعۡبُدُونَ
43:26.en: And when Abraham said unto his father and his folk: Lo! I am innocent of what ye worship

43:27.en: Save Him Who did create me, for He will surely guide me

43:28.ar: وَجَعَلَهَا كَلِمَةَۢ بَاقِيَةࣰ فِي عَقِبِهِۦ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ
43:28.en: And he made it a word enduring among his seed, that haply they might return

43:29.ar: بَلۡ مَتَّعۡتُ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ وَءَابَآءَهُمۡ حَتَّىٰ جَآءَهُمُ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَرَسُولࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
43:29.en: Nay, but I let these and their fathers enjoy life (only) till there should come unto them the Truth and a messenger making plain

43:30.ar: وَلَمَّا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلۡحَقُّ قَالُواْ هَٰذَا سِحۡرࣱ وَإِنَّا بِهِۦ كَٰفِرُونَ
43:30.en: And now that the Truth hath come unto them they say: This is mere magic, and lo! we are disbelievers therein

43:31.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَوۡلَا نُزِّلَ هَٰذَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ عَلَىٰ رَجُلࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡقَرۡيَتَيۡنِ عَظِيمٍ
43:31.en: And they say: If only this Qur'an had been revealed to some great man of the two towns

43:32.ar: أَهُمۡ يَقۡسِمُونَ رَحۡمَتَ رَبِّكَۚ نَحۡنُ قَسَمۡنَا بَيۡنَهُم مَّعِيشَتَهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۚ وَرَفَعۡنَا بَعۡضَهُمۡ فَوۡقَ بَعۡضࣲ دَرَجَٰتࣲ لِّيَتَّخِذَ بَعۡضُهُم بَعۡضࣰ ا سُخۡرِيࣰّ اۗ وَرَحۡمَتُ رَبِّكَ خَيۡرࣱ مِّمَّا يَجۡمَعُونَ
43:32.en: Is it they who apportion thy Lord's mercy? We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of the world, and raised some of them above others in rank that some of them may take labour from others; and the mercy of thy Lord is better than (the wealth) that they amass

43:33.ar: وَلَوۡلَآ أَن يَكُونَ ٱلنَّاسُ أُمَّةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ لَّجَعَلۡنَا لِمَن يَكۡفُرُ بِٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ لِبُيُوتِهِمۡ سُقُفࣰ ا مِّن فِضَّةࣲ وَمَعَارِجَ عَلَيۡهَا يَظۡهَرُونَ
43:33.en: And were it not that mankind would have become one community, We might well have appointed, for those who disbelieve in the Beneficent, roofs of silver for their houses and stairs (of silver) whereby to mount

43:34.ar: وَلِبُيُوتِهِمۡ أَبۡوَٰبࣰ ا وَسُرُرًا عَلَيۡهَا يَتَّكِـُٔونَ
43:34.en: And for their houses doors (of silver) and couches of silver whereon to recline

43:35.ar: وَزُخۡرُفࣰ اۚ وَإِن كُلُّ ذَٰلِكَ لَمَّا مَتَٰعُ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۚ وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةُ عِندَ رَبِّكَ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ
43:35.en: And ornaments of gold. Yet all that would have been but a provision of the life of the world. And the Hereafter with your Lord would have been for those who keep from evil

7:156.ar: ۞وَٱكۡتُبۡ لَنَا فِي هَٰذِهِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا حَسَنَةࣰ وَفِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ إِنَّا هُدۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَۚ قَالَ عَذَابِيٓ أُصِيبُ بِهِۦ مَنۡ أَشَآءُۖ وَرَحۡمَتِي وَسِعَتۡ كُلَّ شَيۡءࣲۚ فَسَأَكۡتُبُهَا لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ وَيُؤۡتُونَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
7:156.en: And ordain for us in this world that which is good, and in the Hereafter (that which is good), Lo! We have turned unto Thee. He said: I smite with My punishment whom I will, and My mercy embraceth all things, therefore I shall ordain it for those who ward off (evil) and pay the poor-due, and those who believe Our revelations

6:12.ar: قُل لِّمَن مَّا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ قُل لِّلَّهِۚ كَتَبَ عَلَىٰ نَفۡسِهِ ٱلرَّحۡمَةَۚ لَيَجۡمَعَنَّكُمۡ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ لَا رَيۡبَ فِيهِۚ ٱلَّذِينَ خَسِرُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ فَهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
6:12.en: Say: Unto whom belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and the earth? Say: Unto Allah. He hath prescribed for Himself mercy, that He may bring you all together to the Day of Resurrection whereof there is no doubt. Those who ruin their souls will not believe

4:76.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱلطَّٰغُوتِ فَقَٰتِلُوٓاْ أَوۡلِيَآءَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِۖ إِنَّ كَيۡدَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ كَانَ ضَعِيفًا
4:76.en: Those who believe do battle for the cause of Allah; and those who disbelieve do battle for the cause of idols. So fight the minions of the devil. Lo! the devil's strategy is ever weak

AmI8Q6zR_S4.speaker: adnan
AmI8Q6zR_S4.speaker_note: listed lecturer is Dr. Adnan Rajeh; weekend Fajr dars continuing his Az-Zukhruf series
AmI8Q6zR_S4.title: Fajr Dars: Az-Zukhruf, Verses 36-45
AmI8Q6zR_S4.one_line: Tafsir of Az-Zukhruf 43:36-45 on the materialist who cannot see the remembrance of al-Rahman, his devil companion, and holding fast whatever the outcome.
AmI8Q6zR_S4.summary: Continuing his reading of Az-Zukhruf, a surah he sees as a warning against a one-dimensional, materialistic view of the world, he explains verses 36 to 45. Zukhruf is what shines outside with no substance inside, and he warns that young people are growing up measuring success only by fame and wealth. The word for turning away from al-Rahman's remembrance describes someone who sees only what shines; such a person is never satisfied and becomes unable to hear spiritual truth. Allah assigns him a devil companion: either a jinn who simply opens a catalogue of temptations suited to his weakness, or, far worse, human companions. He rejects the idea that jinn take over a person and urges that people with psychosis be taken to mental health professionals, not exorcists, recounting a young man who nearly died after an exorcism. Those led astray think they are guided, which he applies to running masajid like businesses instead of as houses of service like the Prophet's masjid with Ahl al-Suffah. The verses then tell the Prophet he cannot make the deaf hear and may die before seeing success, so the true measure is holding fast to revelation on the straight path, for that is what everyone will be asked about.

outline.heading: Opening
Az-Zukhruf: a warning against one-dimensional materialism
outline.gist: The surah, among the Ha-Mim cluster of warnings to those who carry the message, takes on materialism from many angles and is especially relatable today.

outline.heading: Recap: idols, Ibrahim and judging the Prophet by wealth
outline.gist: Earlier verses showed idol worship and the oppression of women driven by profit, blind following of forefathers, Quraysh dismissing the Prophet as not rich, and Allah's statement that He would have given disbelievers silver roofs.

outline.heading: Zukhruf: shine without substance, and how youth measure success
outline.gist: Zukhruf is what glitters outside but has no value inside; we must not let the young judge success only by followers, fame and money.

outline.heading: Why Quranic stories are never repeated identically
outline.gist: Each retelling, including Musa's story coming next, emphasizes what serves its surah's theme, with subtle differences beyond human composition.

outline.heading: Interlude
Turning away from al-Rahman: seeing only what shines
outline.gist: The verb describes one who can see only in bright light; al-Rahman is used because it is a purely spiritual name of all-encompassing mercy.

outline.heading: Materialism is never satisfied
outline.gist: The materialist moves from one shiny thing to the next and would want the moon after owning the planet; we are all susceptible unless we keep reassessing our worldview.

outline.heading: When people can no longer hear it
outline.gist: Some are simply not there yet and need time; others' past choices have closed them off, and all you can do is make dua for them.

outline.heading: The appointed devil: a catalogue of temptations
outline.gist: A jinn devil only keeps showing options until you take one; that is the extent of his power.

outline.heading: No possession: send people to mental health care
outline.gist: He rejects the idea of jinn taking control of a person; such cases need a mental health specialist, not an exorcist, and he will report those who refuse.

outline.heading: The young man harmed by an exorcism
outline.gist: A young man with family schizophrenia was beaten with a radio during an exorcism and nearly took his own life; once told a devil is inside, a paranoid patient can hardly be convinced otherwise.

outline.heading: Families who refuse treatment
outline.gist: Often the family, not the patient, resists care; the community must escalate such cases to save lives.

outline.heading: The devil learns your key
outline.gist: Devils find what you love and open the matching page; for the materialist it is whatever shines, and the companion never leaves.

outline.heading: Human devils are far worse
outline.gist: The plotting of Shaytan is weak, but human companions are relentless, and no one walks into materialism alone.

outline.heading: Led astray while thinking they are guided
outline.gist: The most frightening part is that they believe they are right and everyone else deluded.

outline.heading: A masjid is not a business
outline.gist: A masjid's success cannot be measured in money; it is a house for those who need service, help and serenity among Muslims.

outline.heading: The Prophet's masjid and Ahl al-Suffah
outline.gist: The poorest lived in the Prophet's masjid day and night and he lived beside them; Abu Hurayrah learned so much because he had nothing else to do.

outline.heading: Measured by people, not buildings; what if it's me?
outline.gist: Even with wealth after Mecca they never built it up, because a masjid is its service and love; he fears the verse may describe himself.

outline.heading: Guarding against it with a holistic view
outline.gist: Check that your perspective is healthy and uses more than one metric, so you are not fooled by what shines.

outline.heading: Interlude
Wishing for the distance of the two easts
outline.gist: On the Day of Judgment, with values set right, he wishes he had been as far from his companion as east from west; Arabs name paired things by one of them in the dual.

outline.heading: Shared punishment brings no relief
outline.gist: Disowning your companion then is too late; each is punished for his own wrong.

outline.heading: You cannot make the deaf hear
outline.gist: The Prophet stayed up looking for ways to reach people, but you cannot force sight or hearing on those who chose against it.

outline.heading: You may die before seeing success
outline.gist: In this Meccan surah the Prophet is told he may die before the message triumphs; demanding guaranteed success would itself be a materialistic outlook.

outline.heading: Success is not judged by outcomes
outline.gist: Measure whether work is done properly, not only whether it succeeds, as a prophet who comes on Judgment Day with no followers was still not a failure.

outline.heading: Hold fast to what was revealed
outline.gist: The Prophet's job is to grip revelation like steel and walk the straight path with integrity, which is not closed-mindedness, whether or not fruits appear.

outline.heading: Interlude
The question you will be asked
outline.gist: You will be asked whether you held on and never sold out your values, not how famous or wealthy you became.

outline.heading: Ask the messengers: nothing else is worth worship
outline.gist: Every earlier messenger would say nothing besides Allah was worth worship or devotion; all else is illusion.

outline.heading: Outro

Owm_XdET_RI.title: Surah Summaries: Surat Abasa
Owm_XdET_RI.one_line: Surat Abasa as the Muslim code of conduct: never harm anyone for any reason, and live in constant gratitude.
Owm_XdET_RI.summary: Continuing his summaries of the last juz, he presents Abasa as the third pillar of faith: the code of conduct. He retells the incident with Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum, stressing that the Prophet frowned for a split second, at a blind man who could not see it, and for a noble reason, since he was pursuing the harder task of calling a Quraysh leader. Allah still corrected it, named the surah after it and preserved it until the Day of Judgment. For him this is both proof that no human authored the Quran, because no ego would publish such a thing, and the standard Muslims are held to: no harm to anyone, however small, whatever the reason. He adds that carrying the reminder means honouring the revelation while staying humble and approachable to whoever asks. The second pillar is gratitude: the human being, created from a drop and given a path, still fails to give thanks, while Allah lays out food, water and pasture for him. He ends on the Day of the Blast, when people flee their whole families, reading the fleeing person as someone richly blessed who never showed gratitude. He asks listeners to drop every form of harm and to feel they swim in an ocean of blessings.

outline.heading: Three pillars of faith; Abasa as the code of conduct
outline.gist: Recaps the first group of surahs on what any faith needs: Allah's narrative, the tool and the obstacle, and the code of conduct, which Abasa supplies.

outline.heading: A surah named with a verb: the frown at Ibn Umm Maktum
outline.gist: Abasa is one of two surahs named with a verb. He retells the Prophet speaking to Quraysh leaders when the blind companion called out to him.

outline.heading: Serving the believers before courting the uninterested
outline.gist: The deen obliges us to meet the needs of Muslims who ask before chasing those who do not want the message; the Prophet knew he had to go to Abdullah.

outline.heading: Abdullah never knew: proof the Quran is not human
outline.gist: The blind man only learned of the frown from the surah itself. No human would invent a revelation exposing a moment nobody saw.

outline.heading: He was choosing the harder dawah
outline.gist: Speaking to a hostile audience is harder than to a willing one; the Prophet was reaching for the more difficult, nobler task.

outline.heading: Perhaps he would purify himself
outline.gist: Allah tells him the seeker may benefit and be purified more than the one who turns away.

outline.heading: Imagining the Prophet receiving this surah
outline.gist: He pictures Jibreel reciting it that evening and the Prophet accepting that it would be read for 1400 years; no ego would allow it to be self-authored.

outline.heading: The standard: no frown even at one who cannot see
outline.gist: You may not frown in the face of someone who cannot see it, even for a noble reason. The right act was to go to the caller without the frown.

outline.heading: Named after the incident; a Prophet without ego
outline.gist: The surah is titled 'he frowned'. The Prophet accepted it, honoured Abdullah afterwards, and the passage shows care for people with disabilities. Allah sees even a momentary expression.

outline.heading: A reminder on honoured, purified scrolls
outline.gist: The message is a reminder, not new teaching; whoever wills takes it. Allah elevates both the pages and the noble scribes who carry them.

outline.heading: How ungrateful the human being is
outline.gist: 'Qutila al-insan' as a curse on ingratitude; kufr at root is failure to give thanks. Created from a drop, given a destiny and an eased path, he dies, is resurrected, and has yet to do what he was commanded.

outline.heading: Honour the knowledge, stay humble with people
outline.gist: The carrier of the deen must never cheapen the revelation, yet must not become harsh or hard to approach for anyone who asks.

outline.heading: Gratitude as the second pillar of conduct
outline.gist: The command left unfulfilled is gratitude. Do we see ourselves swimming in an ocean of blessings or fixate on the empty part of the glass?

outline.heading: Always a reason to praise: losing a leg and a son
outline.gist: The early scholar who lost a leg and a son on one day thanked Allah for leaving more than He took.

outline.heading: No form of harm, regardless of reason
outline.gist: After a decade of sacrifice, a single unseen frown was recorded. He cannot understand how Muslims who read this surah go on harming others.

outline.heading: Let him look at his food
outline.gist: Water, grain, grapes, olives, palms and gardens are set up for us and our livestock. The same wording in An-Naziat served humility; here it calls for thanks.

outline.heading: The Day of the Blast: fleeing a full family
outline.gist: The one who flees parents, spouse, siblings and children had been richly blessed but ungrateful; grateful families will hold onto one another. Bright faces and dust-covered faces.

outline.heading: Two things that define a Muslim
outline.gist: Conduct and gratitude: remember the story of the frown and remember to be grateful.

outline.heading: Outro

QJzCxG2xbRs.title: Surah Summaries: Al-Buruj
QJzCxG2xbRs.one_line: Al-Buruj teaches that passivity is a choice: the people of the trench condemned include the bystanders who watched and said nothing.
QJzCxG2xbRs.summary: Al-Buruj closes the group of surahs on choice with its hardest lesson: doing nothing is itself a decision. After recalling the well-known story of a tyrant who burned believers in a fire-filled trench, he argues from the wording that the 'people of the trench' who are cursed include those who sat by and witnessed it, since the Quran uses the idea of sitting for holding back from a duty. The bystander mentality, minding your own business while atrocities unfold, is a modern Muslim problem made worse by phones that let everyone watch suffering and scroll past. He quotes a teacher who found the surah's most hopeful words in 'then did not repent': even the torturers were offered tawbah, and their only path to it was witnesses speaking up. Silence fed Pharaoh's belief in his own divinity, and speaking the truth can save the oppressor as well as the oppressed. Soldiers who say they only follow orders and Thamud's indifference born of wealth make the same point. Knowing the truth but not standing for it is a form of denial. He calls the audience to value their choices and refuse indifference.

outline.heading: Recap: what the group on choice has taught
outline.gist: Choice is sacred, accountable, recorded, has consequences, and its margin is narrow, so choose with knowledge.

outline.heading: The story of the trench

outline.heading: Oaths by the constellations, the promised day, witness and witnessed
outline.gist: The rising constellations contrast with the trench below; the oath covers every witness and everything ever witnessed.

outline.heading: Who are the people of the trench?
outline.gist: Not only the ones who threw believers into the fuelled fire; the torturers are addressed later.

outline.heading: Qu'ud: sitting back from a duty
outline.gist: In the Quran, as in At-Tawbah, sitting means staying back from what you should have done; they sat by it watching.

outline.heading: The bystander mentality
outline.gist: They witnessed what was done to the believers. Today Muslims say it is not their problem and turn a blind eye, thinking not committing the crime exempts them.

outline.heading: Cursed for watching; Allah witnessed them witnessing
outline.gist: They had a chance to speak and defend the oppressed and did not. The believers' only crime was faith in the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, who owns the heavens and witnesses all.

outline.heading: The believers who held to their choice are the winners
outline.gist: Those burned for their faith achieved the greatest success. The enemy of love and empathy is indifference.

outline.heading: We are all witnesses now
outline.gist: Criminals are few; the ninety percent watch. We have the means to film starvation and oppression from many angles but not to stop it, and we scroll past.

outline.heading: 'Then did not repent': the most hopeful words
outline.gist: His teacher's most hopeful verse: even the torturers were offered tawbah, and their only path to it was someone speaking up.

outline.heading: Silence made Pharaoh
outline.gist: Haman and those around him kept affirming him until he believed he was god. Your life is never weighed against the truth.

outline.heading: Speaking up can save the oppressor too
outline.gist: Standing for what is right may save the oppressor from himself as well as the oppressed.

outline.heading: Your Lord's grip is severe; He does what He wills
outline.gist: Allah originates and repeats, forgives and loves, owns the throne and is not questioned; our task is to learn to stand for what is right.

outline.heading: The soldiers: just following orders
outline.gist: The armies of Pharaoh and Thamud are named because soldiers are the ultimate bystanders who claim no control.

outline.heading: Thamud: the everlasting example of indifference
outline.gist: Too much wealth and no early responsibility breed people who care about nothing and see atrocities as a joke.

outline.heading: Refusing to stand for truth is a form of denial
outline.gist: Takdhib runs through all these surahs; knowing what is right and not defending the oppressed or opposing racism is denial in another form.

outline.heading: Allah encompasses them; you cannot leave the pitch
outline.gist: Every choice and every non-choice is surrounded by Allah; there is no 'I had nothing to do with it'.

outline.heading: A glorious Quran; why this group matters
outline.gist: The preserved Quran speaks to people who value their decisions; he summarises the whole group on choice.

46fccIDRAUY.title: Surah Summaries: Al-Muddaththir and Al-Qiyamah
46fccIDRAUY.one_line: Al-Muddaththir on outward representation and the four answers from Saqar, then Al-Qiyamah as dawah to the intellect through conscience and insight.
46fccIDRAUY.summary: The sheikh finishes Al-Muddaththir, the surah of how a believer carries the message outwardly after Al-Muzzammil's inner preparation. Its first commands cover purity of appearance and soul and perseverance, and it shows a man who rejected the truth out of self-interest. Its remark on the number of Hell's keepers exposes a fixation on details that change no one's behaviour, which he turns into a test for any dawah topic. The people of Saqar give four reasons for being there: no prayer, not feeding the needy, drifting with the crowd, and denying the Day. He warns against cherry-picking them, since half of Islam is serving people and a believer must hold his own principles. Al-Qiyamah then opens the cluster's three models of dawah by addressing the intellect. Allah swears by the self-blaming conscience, whose death leaves a sociopath. People doubt resurrection because they want to sin without guilt, yet every person has full insight into himself and can win arguments with excuses but not before Allah. Loving the world is fine unless it pushes out the hereafter. The only blessing the surah names is seeing Allah's face, a joy beyond imagination. It ends by asking whether man thinks he is left aimless.

outline.heading: Inner and outer: Muzzammil and Muddaththir
outline.gist: Al-Muzzammil gives the soul what it needs to continue the journey; Al-Muddaththir, named for the outer cloak, shows how the believer appears to people. Its opening commands were among the first the Prophet heard.

outline.heading: Refusing the truth out of self-interest
outline.gist: The commands to purify appearance and soul, avoid moral impurity and persevere are followed by a man who rejected what he knew was right for personal gain, which a carrier of the message can never afford.

outline.heading: Details that change no one's behaviour
outline.gist: Allah exposes the pagans' fixation on meaningless detail. A compass for dawah: if a topic will not improve people's outlooks or behaviour, talk about something else.

outline.heading: An answer from Saqar: we did not pray
outline.gist: A question is put to people in Hell and we hear their reply, the most frightening testimony one could listen to.

outline.heading: We did not feed the needy
outline.gist: Few would think this keeps one from Hell, yet the Quran says it. Half of Islam is deeds that serve other people; neglecting that half is not an option.

outline.heading: We went with the flow
outline.gist: They drifted with whatever people did and talked of whatever was talked about. The Prophet forbade being one who is good only when people are good.

outline.heading: I am only one of my tribe
outline.gist: The pre-Islamic mindset: if my tribe errs I err. A believer must decide on his principles and commit to them.

outline.heading: Do not cherry-pick the four
outline.gist: Prayer, feeding the needy, holding firm principles and belief in the Day form a template of ritual, empathy and integrity; perfecting two and neglecting two puts you at risk.

outline.heading: Three surahs, three ways of dawah
outline.gist: The juz's last three surahs model dawah: one through reward, one through warning of punishment, and Al-Qiyamah through the intellect.

outline.heading: The earthly part and the higher part
outline.gist: When the spirit met the soil-based body, a self was born with earthly traits that respond to reward and fear. That works and matters, but it speaks to the primitive part.

outline.heading: Speaking to the spirit
outline.gist: Al-Qiyamah addresses the part of us that grasps deep concepts beyond pleasure and pain, which is why people love it.

outline.heading: The self-blaming soul is your conscience
outline.gist: The nagging voice that knows you are doing wrong is a higher faculty from the spirit; it feels guilt and blames itself.

outline.heading: A dead conscience
outline.gist: Psychologists describe a sociopath as someone whose conscience died. Tigers feel no guilt over the gazelle; humans must bring conscience into decisions.

outline.heading: Bones, fingerprints and bal
outline.gist: Does man think the One who created him cannot rebuild him to his fingerprints? Bal, two letters that carry a sentence, says that is not the real problem.

outline.heading: The wish to sin without guilt
outline.gist: Except those Allah has purified, everyone harbours a wish to live out every fantasy unwatched; much disbelief comes back to not wanting Allah's limits.

outline.heading: When is the Day? Nowhere to hide
outline.gist: Eyes dazzled, moon dimmed, sun and moon joined: man asks where to run, and the only destination is standing before his Lord.

outline.heading: Shown what took you forward and back
outline.gist: Every deed that moved you forward or pulled you back will be explained; then another bal names the deeper problem.

outline.heading: Full insight: turn your vision inward
outline.gist: Basar belongs to the eyes and basirah to the heart. You do not need life coaches; shift focus from analysing others to analysing yourself.

outline.heading: You can win any argument with excuses
outline.gist: No one can out-argue your reasons for not changing, just as a child has his excuse list ready, but inside you know when you are making it up.

outline.heading: Excuses will not work before Allah
outline.gist: You need no one watching over you, only to focus your sight and stop gathering excuses; you may convince people, but not Allah.

outline.heading: Two readings of do not move your tongue
outline.gist: The verses may address the Prophet receiving revelation, which is valid, or, more in keeping with the flow, the person whose book is being read to him and who rushes past uncomfortable pages.

outline.heading: Follow along; We will clarify
outline.gist: Allah tells him to stop rushing: We compiled it, We recite it, follow along, and We will clarify anything he objects to.

outline.heading: Swearing falsely to Allah
outline.gist: Those who die without facing themselves will swear to Allah they did not do what they did, as they did in this world, convinced they have a case.

outline.heading: Your own body testifies
outline.gist: We can lie to ourselves until we believe it; then every part of the body will testify, though deep down the person always knew the truth.

outline.heading: Loving this world is not the problem
outline.gist: Loving life, people and achievements is fine; the problem is pairing it with neglect of the hereafter.

outline.heading: When it is the only love you have
outline.gist: We are not meant to hate the world. The danger is when love of it dictates every decision while the hereafter, a few steps away, is ignored.

outline.heading: The one blessing that needs a higher mind
outline.gist: Most descriptions of Paradise are tangible; the only one here is faces looking at their Lord, which has no parallel and must not be imagined, fitting a surah that addresses the intellect.

outline.heading: The lowest in Paradise
outline.gist: The last person out of Hell is given a dominion many times the size of the earth, enough to spend a thousand years exploring.

outline.heading: Those who see Him twice a day
outline.gist: The highest ranks see Allah morning and evening and find nothing more beautiful; all beauty has one source, so think bigger than the fruits of Paradise.

outline.heading: Dark faces and the hour of parting
outline.gist: Other faces frown, dreading a humiliating blow. At death, medicine reaches its limit and the person knows it is time to part.

outline.heading: He neither believed nor prayed
outline.gist: Shin entwined with shin is an Arabic phrase for things turning grave. Driven to his Lord, he is reminded that he turned from what he knew was true and went home jolly, taking it lightly.

outline.heading: Far better had you prioritized differently
outline.gist: The repeated phrase stresses how much better it would have been with insight switched on and priorities straight. The whole surah is a ready dawah for anyone willing to think.

outline.heading: Where is the intellect in that?
outline.gist: Does man think he will be left aimless? The One who brought him from a drop to a conscious, balanced being can surely do it again.

43:20.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَوۡ شَآءَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ مَا عَبَدۡنَٰهُمۗ مَّا لَهُم بِذَٰلِكَ مِنۡ عِلۡمٍۖ إِنۡ هُمۡ إِلَّا يَخۡرُصُونَ
43:20.en: And they say: If the Beneficent One had (so) willed, we should not have worshipped them. They have no knowledge whatsoever of that. They do but guess

43:21.ar: أَمۡ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُمۡ كِتَٰبࣰ ا مِّن قَبۡلِهِۦ فَهُم بِهِۦ مُسۡتَمۡسِكُونَ
43:21.en: Or have We given them any scripture before (this Qur'an) so that they are holding fast thereto

43:22.ar: بَلۡ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا وَجَدۡنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا عَلَىٰٓ أُمَّةࣲ وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِهِم مُّهۡتَدُونَ
43:22.en: Nay, for they say only: Lo! we found our fathers following a religion, and we are guided by their footprints

43:23.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ مَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مِن قَبۡلِكَ فِي قَرۡيَةࣲ مِّن نَّذِيرٍ إِلَّا قَالَ مُتۡرَفُوهَآ إِنَّا وَجَدۡنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا عَلَىٰٓ أُمَّةࣲ وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِهِم مُّقۡتَدُونَ
43:23.en: And even so We sent not a warner before thee (Muhammad) into any township but its luxurious ones said: Lo! we found our fathers following a religion, and we are following their footprints

43:24.ar: ۞قَٰلَ أَوَلَوۡ جِئۡتُكُم بِأَهۡدَىٰ مِمَّا وَجَدتُّمۡ عَلَيۡهِ ءَابَآءَكُمۡۖ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا بِمَآ أُرۡسِلۡتُم بِهِۦ كَٰفِرُونَ
43:24.en: (And the warner) said: What! Even though I bring you better guidance than that ye found your fathers following? They answered: Lo! in what ye bring we are disbelievers

43:25.ar: فَٱنتَقَمۡنَا مِنۡهُمۡۖ فَٱنظُرۡ كَيۡفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلۡمُكَذِّبِينَ
43:25.en: So We requited them. Then see the nature of the consequence for the rejecters

43:26.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوۡمِهِۦٓ إِنَّنِي بَرَآءࣱ مِّمَّا تَعۡبُدُونَ
43:26.en: And when Abraham said unto his father and his folk: Lo! I am innocent of what ye worship

43:27.en: Save Him Who did create me, for He will surely guide me

43:28.ar: وَجَعَلَهَا كَلِمَةَۢ بَاقِيَةࣰ فِي عَقِبِهِۦ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ
43:28.en: And he made it a word enduring among his seed, that haply they might return

43:29.ar: بَلۡ مَتَّعۡتُ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ وَءَابَآءَهُمۡ حَتَّىٰ جَآءَهُمُ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَرَسُولࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
43:29.en: Nay, but I let these and their fathers enjoy life (only) till there should come unto them the Truth and a messenger making plain

43:30.ar: وَلَمَّا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلۡحَقُّ قَالُواْ هَٰذَا سِحۡرࣱ وَإِنَّا بِهِۦ كَٰفِرُونَ

TAQQk3gny_8.speaker_note: Fajr dars series at Muslim Wellness Network credited to Dr. Adnan Rajeh; refers to his own sessions earlier in the week
TAQQk3gny_8.title: Az-Zukhruf, Verses 20-30 (Fajr Dars)
TAQQk3gny_8.one_line: The fatalist excuse and free will, speaking for Allah without knowledge, blind loyalty to ancestral custom, and Ibrahim leaving a lasting word behind.
TAQQk3gny_8.summary: He recaps the surah's warning against one-dimensional materialistic thinking, recalling how early Muslims stood out for honouring women while today consumer culture teaches young people that only wealth and fame mean success. Verse 20's claim that the idolaters worship by Allah's will is the old fatalist argument: it assumes Allah knows the future the way we do, by programming, as with a wind-up car or the failed pandemic projections. Allah knows every possible choice while we remain free. Verse 21's demand for a book leads him to the gravity of speaking on Allah's behalf, his own greatest fear as a teacher, and to the hadith of the man who swore Allah would not forgive another: no one may use the Quran as a catalogue of who goes to Hell. Verses 22-25 show the affluent always defending ancestral custom because it serves them, which he sees today in costly cultural marriage customs that leave young people unmarried into their thirties. Islam was never rejected on theology alone; there is always a personal hook. The mukadhdhib saw the truth and refused it, unlike someone shown a distorted Islam. Ibrahim rejected the rigged religion of Ur and left a word behind as a seed, the model for persistent, patient dawah, even with teenagers who seem not to listen.

outline.heading: Recap: the Ha-Mim cluster and its three warnings
outline.gist: Surahs sharing the same opening letters share a theme; Az-Zukhruf warns against what glitters without substance and the one-dimensional materialistic view behind much bad judgment.

outline.heading: Recap: women valued only for financial benefit
outline.gist: In Jahiliyyah women were devalued because they did not add warriors or wealth to the tribe, a mentality the Quran changed.

outline.heading: When Muslims led on women's rights
outline.gist: A Muslim of the Prophet's era stood out for how he treated women: rights to believe, learn, voice an opinion, inherit, own and trade, and equal accountability before Allah, long before other societies. Muslims have since regressed.

outline.heading: Consumer culture is framing young minds
outline.gist: The same narrow outlook rules today, which is why he chose this surah; consumerism is shaping what young people hope for, fear and call success.

outline.heading: Your father still made it
outline.gist: A father without a million followers who worked hard and held a family together is a success; making wealth and fame the only markers is a calamity, and the Quran addresses this head on.

outline.heading: If the Most Merciful had willed: the fatalist excuse
outline.gist: After reciting, he explains their claim that they worship idols by Allah's will, the age-old argument of compulsion, which ignores that Allah can create a creature with free will.

outline.heading: Free will is no threat to Allah
outline.gist: Nothing the creature does escapes Him; the materialist can only judge by his own simple experience, so the verse says they are merely guessing.

outline.heading: Kharas: the farmer's estimate
outline.gist: Kharas is how farmers back home estimated the fruit on a tree to pay the landowner up front, a guess rather than a count; their claim is just as unfounded.

outline.heading: We can only predict what has no choice
outline.gist: We foresee only what follows an algorithm, like a wind-up car aimed at a pillar; forecasts of human behaviour remain estimates that people keep breaking.

outline.heading: The pandemic and the limits of prediction
outline.gist: Two years of failed graphs and projections eroded trust in the medical system and governments, showing how little we can predict.

outline.heading: He knows, yet you are free
outline.gist: If Allah's knowledge worked like ours the fatalists would be right; it does not, and that difference is exactly what makes Him God.

outline.heading: Every possible option is known to Him
outline.gist: Borrowing the idea of infinite parallel universes: Allah knows every option open to you at each moment, and you simply choose among them, so you can never surprise Him.

outline.heading: Did We give them a book before this?
outline.gist: Their claim rests on no knowledge and no scripture; Allah asks where it came from.

outline.heading: The danger of speaking for Allah
outline.gist: Attributing to Allah what is untrue or unknown is among the gravest sins; anyone explaining the Quran must think a hundred times, because a mistake spreads and letting ego or agenda in is the worst corruption.

outline.heading: Who gave you permission?
outline.gist: Allah challenges them to show the book that says He compels people, and asks who authorised them to speak on His behalf.

outline.heading: The man who swore Allah would not forgive
outline.gist: Allah forgave the sinner and held the one who spoke for Him to account; reciting a warning is very different from applying it to people.

outline.heading: The Quran is not a catalogue of the damned
outline.gist: Syllogisms like 'every mushrik enters the Fire, so this person will' do not apply; declaring someone's destination puts you at terrible risk.

outline.heading: Where people end up is Allah's business
outline.gist: We may only name a destination Allah or the Prophet named, as with Abu Lahab; the next verse turns to their real motive.

outline.heading: We found our fathers on a way
outline.gist: Their real problem was the ease of the status quo, especially when it is inherited and financially beneficial; then it becomes almost impossible to change.

outline.heading: Custom outlives even harm
outline.gist: Even harmful cultural traditions resist change; ummah here means a collective way of life the forefathers lived.

outline.heading: The affluent always resist the warner
outline.gist: Every warner was opposed first by the comfortable, who did not care who was oppressed so long as it was not them; the pattern persists today in new forms.

outline.heading: Marriage held hostage by culture
outline.gist: Cultural costs and celebrations leave men and women unmarried into their thirties, though the Prophet married people with Quran as the dowry.

outline.heading: The question no one asks
outline.gist: Delaying marriage fifteen years past puberty while turning a blind eye, for the sake of family prestige, is worse than Jahiliyyah because we know the alternative.

outline.heading: Complaining about mahr, then demanding it
outline.gist: A father protests the dowry demanded for his son, then years later imposes the same on his daughter's suitor: the same materialistic logic.

outline.heading: Even if I brought better guidance?
outline.gist: Every warner offered something better than ancestral habit, and they replied they reject whatever he was sent with without hearing it.

outline.heading: Islam was never rejected on theology
outline.gist: Like Salih's people, they refused because change threatened prestige and income; he finds no case in the Quran or Sunnah of rejection on theology alone.

outline.heading: Find the hook
outline.gist: In his conversations with doubters he looks for the personal experience or misunderstanding behind the objection, because the theology of one Creator beyond time and space is simple and beautiful.

outline.heading: The mukadhdhib saw the truth and refused it
outline.gist: Unlike the general term kafir, the mukadhdhib recognised the right way and refused it for self-interest, which earns the severest punishment.

outline.heading: Those shown a distorted Islam
outline.gist: People who rejected a badly presented Islam will likely find mercy; we deal with others at face value but cannot know their backstory or judge their end.

outline.heading: Ibrahim's Ur, the great city of its age
outline.gist: He recites Ibrahim's verses and describes Ur in southern Iraq near today's Nasiriyah, a crowded centre of knowledge and power with temple-towers built on high ground.

outline.heading: A rigged religion of kings and clergy
outline.gist: Gods of moon, sun and rain, some reachable only through costly offerings to priests, kept everyone controlled; Ibrahim saw it as a game run by liars.

outline.heading: Free of what you worship, except my Creator
outline.gist: Ibrahim disowned their gods except the One who created him and will guide him; they expelled him, yet he left those words behind him.

outline.heading: Breaking the idols
outline.gist: Their offerings fed corrupt clergy and kings; he broke the idols, left the axe on the biggest, and exposed that they worship what cannot speak.

outline.heading: Leave a seed behind
outline.gist: They knew they were wrong but too much was at stake, so they threw him in the fire; still he left a lasting word, and that is the Muslim's duty in dawah.

outline.heading: Teenagers who come back years later
outline.gist: Youth work can be draining when they mock and ignore you, but people he had given up on returned years later recalling his words; say the genuine, kind word anyway.

outline.heading: Comfort as the real obstacle
outline.gist: Ibrahim is the model, and the surah's point is that the people were embedded in inherited wealth and comfort when the clear messenger came.

outline.heading: They called the truth magic
outline.gist: Their rejection followed their financial interest, another example of materialistic judgment.

BUNPxsw3acQ.title: Surah Summaries: Surat Al-A'la
BUNPxsw3acQ.one_line: Al-A'la gives the second tool, tasbih: exalting Allah above any flaw, so that in tragedy we look to ourselves and never blame Him.
BUNPxsw3acQ.summary: After recapping the first tool, tawakkul, he presents Al-A'la's tool: tasbih, far broader than counting on the fingers. Before Islam the word meant doing something abundantly, from the root for swimming; in Islam it means declaring Allah free of any flaw, mistake or blame. Allah is exalted whether we say it or not, so we glorify His name for our own hearts. The surah gives four angles for building this conviction: studying the universe, from the precise design of creation to DNA coding all of life's history; acknowledging that humans forget and err constantly; understanding that Allah eased us toward the easiest path, so if religion feels hard the fault lies with us and preachers who make it seem impossible misrepresent Allah; and purifying the self. He tells of breaking news of stage four lung cancer to a fit non-smoker who campaigned against smoking, and says the first urge in such moments is to blame God. Blaming Allah after an undeserved hardship, he says, is the leading cause of people losing faith, more than atheism. Prophet Isa, asked about those who worshipped him, began with 'Glory be to You.' He urges people to rehearse tasbih daily so it is their first response when life knocks them down.

outline.heading: Tasbih is more than counting on fingers
outline.gist: Dhikr after prayer is good, but tasbih is a worldview that distinguishes a Muslim from everyone else.

outline.heading: From swimming to exalting Allah above any flaw
outline.gist: Before Islam the word meant doing something abundantly, from the root for swimming; in Islam it means denying any flaw, error or blame in Allah.

outline.heading: Exalt the name: for your own heart
outline.gist: Allah does not benefit from our worship; we exalt His name so that it is exalted in our own minds.

outline.heading: He created, proportioned, decreed and guided
outline.gist: Every creature fits the larger mosaic and knows its way within days, while humans take decades.

outline.heading: First angle: looking at the universe
outline.gist: Pasture turning to dark stubble and back; the deeper we look through microscope and telescope, the clearer His perfection, down to DNA coding all of life's history.

outline.heading: Second angle: we are the flawed ones
outline.gist: 'You will not forget, except what Allah wills': humans forget and err constantly; when things go wrong, look first at what we could have done better.

outline.heading: The urge to blame: a lung cancer diagnosis
outline.gist: Breaking news of spread cancer to a fit non-smoker; the first urge is to blame someone, and Shaytan points upward. A Muslim never blames Allah.

outline.heading: Blaming God: the top cause of lost faith
outline.gist: More people lose faith through undeserved hardship than through atheism. Subhanallah is said when facing what you cannot explain, then you look at your own part.

outline.heading: Third angle: We will ease you toward ease
outline.gist: If the path feels hard, the difficulty is in us: no discipline, wanting shortcuts. Allah prepared us for the easiest path.

outline.heading: A preacher must not make Islam seem impossible
outline.gist: Portraying the deen as near impossible accuses Allah of an unfair design. His commands are within our ability and make life better here too.

outline.heading: Ease here leads to ease there
outline.gist: The choice is not hardship now for ease later; obedience brings ease in both worlds and disobedience brings misery in both.

outline.heading: The reverent remember; the most wretched turn away
outline.gist: The one who refuses the reminder chooses lasting misery; the wealthy sinner is not truly happy, since true happiness is serenity and meaning.

outline.heading: Neither dying nor living in the Fire
outline.gist: Those in Hell wish to die and cannot, yet their state cannot be called life.

outline.heading: Fourth angle: purifying the self
outline.gist: Success comes to the one who purifies within and remembers his Lord and prays; an arrogant, doubtful or oblivious self cannot live tasbih.

outline.heading: The patient's story concluded
outline.gist: He came in for a suspected broken rib and was found to have advanced cancer; imagine that moment with empathy.

outline.heading: Isa's answer: Glory be to You
outline.gist: A prophet who taught tawhid all his life, asked about those who worshipped him, begins by exalting Allah and blames no one but leaves them to His mercy.

outline.heading: Rehearse it daily for the day you fall
outline.gist: We say tasbih for our own sake so it is the first thing out of our mouths when life knocks us down.

outline.heading: You prefer this world, though the Hereafter is better
outline.gist: The self dislikes blame and looks for someone else to hang mistakes on; the root is loving this life too much.

outline.heading: In the scriptures of Ibrahim and Musa
outline.gist: Tasbih has been taught since Ibrahim and before; it protects us from ever blaming God.

TQYFBMlClDg.title: Surah Summaries: Al-Mutaffifin and Al-Inshiqaq
TQYFBMlClDg.one_line: Al-Mutaffifin: choices are recorded and have consequences in both worlds. Al-Inshiqaq: our margin of choice is narrow, so choose well.
TQYFBMlClDg.summary: Continuing the group of surahs on choice, he reads Al-Mutaffifin as a warning against double standards: taking your full due while shortchanging others, or exempting yourself from rules you impose on everyone else, including in matters of chastity. The surah then stresses that every deed is written in a numbered record. He works through simple arithmetic to show that a lifetime of about 30,000 days is easy to document. Consequences come in this life too: repeated sin coats the heart until it loses insight, cannot tell halal from haram and drifts from faith, and in the next life the deniers are veiled from their Lord. The righteous have faces glowing with ease, a sealed drink and a spring beyond imagination, which is worth competing for, and even a passing moment of mockery will be fairly recompensed. Al-Inshiqaq adds a twist: the sky and earth obey without choice, every human labours toward meeting Allah whatever path he takes, and much of life is predetermined. What remains are perhaps a hundred thousand real decisions, about values, motives and ethics, and they shape later generations. He asks listeners to make those few choices carefully and with knowledge.

outline.heading: Recap: choices are sacred and accountable
outline.gist: The first group gave the pillars of faith; At-Takwir and Al-Infitar said choice is a holy right and carries accountability. Today: choices are recorded and have consequences.

outline.heading: Woe to the defrauders: double standards
outline.gist: Those who take full measure for themselves and give less to others stand for every double standard and self-made exception.

outline.heading: Exempting yourself: the chastity example
outline.gist: People who rationalise breaking laws they demand of others do not expect to be resurrected; the man who polices how others treat his family but allows himself the same.

outline.heading: Sijjin: the inscribed record of the wicked
outline.gist: The record of those who turned away lies in a confined place, a numbered, written book; he explains the Quran's 'what will make you know' pattern.

outline.heading: Transgressor and sinner: two kinds of wrong
outline.gist: Some wrongs harm only oneself and some harm others, just as good deeds do; the denier of accountability commits both and calls revelation old tales.

outline.heading: Consequences arrive in this life too
outline.gist: Allah's commands benefit us and His prohibitions protect us here as well as in the Hereafter.

outline.heading: Rayn: hearts covered by what they earned
outline.gist: Denial is not about logic; the heart, not the eye, goes blind when sin covers it.

outline.heading: Black spots on the heart and loss of insight
outline.gist: Each sin leaves a dark spot until the heart cannot take in light, halal feels haram and haram feels halal, and faith slips away.

outline.heading: Veiled from their Lord
outline.gist: In the Hereafter the deniers are deprived of seeing Allah, then enter Hell and are told this is what they denied.

outline.heading: Illiyyin: the record of the righteous
outline.gist: The righteous have their own numbered book, witnessed by the angels closest to Allah.

outline.heading: A lifetime is only 30,000 pages
outline.gist: A thousand months is about 30,000 days and a few hundred thousand waking hours; keeping record of it is easy, and life is short.

outline.heading: Faces radiant with ease; a sealed nectar
outline.gist: We read a loved one's day on their face; Allah points us to the faces of the people of Paradise and their drink sealed with musk.

outline.heading: Let the competitors compete for this
outline.gist: Reserve your place in an endless life rather than competing over a short one.

outline.heading: Tasnim: pleasures beyond imagining
outline.gist: A spring we have never heard of shows that Paradise holds delights we cannot conceive.

outline.heading: The mockers and the mocked
outline.gist: Those who laughed at believers will see the tables turned; even a forgotten moment of mockery has fair consequences.

outline.heading: Al-Inshiqaq: the margin of choice is narrow
outline.gist: After saying choices are sacred, accountable and recorded, this surah reminds us we do not choose from an infinite ocean of options, so choose with knowledge.

outline.heading: Sky and earth heed their Lord
outline.gist: Things we think have no choice are portrayed as listening and obeying, turning the tables on us.

outline.heading: Toiling toward your Lord, whatever the path
outline.gist: Every human labours toward some goal, even the gamer at home, and every path ends standing before Allah.

outline.heading: Within the labour: values, motives and ethics
outline.gist: The real choices are why we work, what values and ethics we carry and what goals we pursue; the believer gets an easy reckoning.

outline.heading: The record behind the back
outline.gist: The one who knew but did not act tries to hide his hand, yet the record reaches his left hand behind his back; deep down we all know.

outline.heading: Only about a hundred thousand decisions
outline.gist: Origins, family and looks are given; a few decisions a day over a lifetime are all we truly make.

outline.heading: He thought he would never return
outline.gist: Once happy among his family, he did not believe enough to live by it, and now calls for his own destruction.

outline.heading: Oaths by twilight, night and the full moon
outline.gist: The passage of dawn, night and moon pictures time moving forward.

outline.heading: Stage after stage: choices shape future generations
outline.gist: Each generation walks a path passed down by the last; our choices affect people long after us. Why do they not prostrate?

outline.heading: Choose your few choices well
outline.gist: A short close: the margin is small, so make each decision carefully.

6Kl3VmJjXic.title: Surah Summaries: Surat Al-Muzzammil
6Kl3VmJjXic.one_line: Al-Muzzammil as the fuel for a lifetime of carrying the deen: night prayer, Quran, dhikr, devotion, patience and leaving harmful company beautifully.
6Kl3VmJjXic.summary: Pairing Al-Muzzammil with Al-Muddaththir, he says this surah answers how someone carrying Islam for seventy years keeps going without burning out. Addressed by a name used only once, recalling the Prophet asking to be wrapped after the first revelation, it concerns the personal side of the caller. A sequence of commands follows: stand the night, recite the Quran slowly enough to absorb it, remember Allah, devote yourself to Him alone, bear what people say patiently, and leave those who drag you down with a departure that is beautiful, without burning bridges. Between them stands the warning of a heavy word: the road will be hard and many will want to quit, as he admits he nearly has. His central point is that prayer is fuel, not a burden: the more you pray the more you recharge for a demanding day. The Prophet is sent as a witness, meaning a living example that removes every excuse. Intentions loosen over time and must be tightened again. The final Madinan verse eases the night prayer but keeps the command to read what is easy, because without the Quran the soul dries up.

outline.gist: The Prophet was told up front the message is heavy; expect disappointment, failure and discouraging words.

outline.heading: Salah is fuel, not a burden

outline.heading: The more you pray, the more you charge

outline.heading: Command three: remember the name of your Lord
outline.gist: Dhikr does not add to Allah; it keeps your own heart close to living Islam fully.

outline.heading: Command four: devote yourself to Him alone
outline.gist: Tabattul is full sincerity, embodied in sujood; offer yourself to no one but Allah.

outline.heading: Command five: patience with what they say
outline.gist: Prayer done right gives the strength to withstand doubts and discouragement.

outline.heading: Command six: leave them with a beautiful departure
outline.gist: Walk away from those who pull you astray without cursing, gossip or animosity.

outline.heading: Recognise who holds you back; do not burn bridges
outline.gist: Some will push you forward and some will sow doubts and laziness; step away from the latter while keeping doors open.

outline.heading: Sent as a witness, as to Pharaoh
outline.gist: Shahid means a living example, like the example verse a grammarian cites to prove a rule.

outline.heading: The example removes every excuse
outline.gist: No one can claim the Quran is impossible to live when the Prophet lived it; the martyr is a witness in the same sense.

outline.heading: Without fuel you burn out
outline.gist: The mosque is full for the first nights of Ramadan and empties as the self tires.

outline.heading: Tighten your intentions again and again
outline.gist: Good intentions loosen as life shakes them; screw them back down or they fly off.

outline.heading: A day that turns children grey
outline.gist: Allah describes the reaction rather than the sight: children's hair whitens and the sky splits.

outline.heading: The last verse, revealed years later in Madinah
outline.gist: Its length shows a much later revelation that eases the measure of night prayer.

outline.heading: Read what is easy: the Quran as nourishment
outline.gist: Illness, work and struggle are acknowledged, but stop reading and the soul dries up; make the Quran add to you.

outline.heading: Whatever good you send ahead, and seeking forgiveness
outline.gist: What you do for yourself you will find multiplied with Allah; seek forgiveness because these commands are hard.

cHS16IPpyJc.title: Surah Summaries: Surat At-Tariq
cHS16IPpyJc.one_line: At-Tariq opens the third group of Juz Amma, the believer's toolkit, with its first tool: tawakkul, explained in three elements.
cHS16IPpyJc.summary: He introduces the third group of surahs in the last juz as seven tools that a Muslim can only learn from revelation, unlike social concepts that common sense can reach. The first tool, in At-Tariq, is tawakkul, explained without being named. Allah swears by the sky and a piercing star, which he connects to stars and supernovas that could wipe out a solar system in seconds. We do not lie awake fearing such forces, yet we worry endlessly about illness and accidents, sometimes to the point of anxiety disorders. The answer is that every soul has a guardian over it for its appointed time. He then reminds listeners of their humble origin from a gushing fluid, their return, and a day when secrets are exposed and no one has power or helper. After many surahs with no commands, the surah ends with two: give them respite, gently. From all this he draws three elements of tawakkul: inner dependence on Allah for outcomes, exhausting your own effort, illustrated by the student who studies versus the one who crams and expects a miracle, and accepting whatever result comes. He asks listeners to stop wasting energy on worry, do their job fully and be content with Allah's decision.

outline.heading: Recap: pillars of faith and the group on choice
outline.gist: Juz Amma summarises Islam's core concepts; the first group gave the pillars, the second covered every angle of choice.

outline.heading: The third group: tools only revelation can teach
outline.gist: Commanding good and forbidding wrong are social concepts; halal and haram exist only within faith. The next seven surahs each give a religious tool.

outline.heading: Tools that change how you see the world
outline.gist: Memorising and reflecting on these seven tools reshapes how you perceive yourself and carry yourself.

outline.heading: The night-comer: the piercing star
outline.gist: Tariq is one who knocks at night; it is explained as the piercing star that leaves a void. The companions understood it as a star that can cause harm.

outline.heading: Supernovas and our fragility
outline.gist: Stars have life cycles; some release enough energy to destroy a solar system. The more we study space, the smaller we are.

outline.heading: Every soul has a guardian over it
outline.gist: No one worries about a distant star; every soul is preserved for the time Allah gives it.

outline.heading: Daily variables and the trap of worry
outline.gist: Illness and accidents can strike us or loved ones at any moment; some people become anxious or compulsive. Since Allah preserves each soul for its term, worry wastes energy.

outline.heading: Tawakkul explained before it is named
outline.gist: This early surah teaches the concept the companions had only heard as a word; whoever grasps and practises tawakkul holds most of the deen.

outline.heading: A humble beginning from a gushing fluid
outline.gist: We came from something lowly and grew into power and influence; He who began us will bring us back.

outline.heading: The day secrets are laid bare
outline.gist: Tubla means exposed: hidden thoughts we fully control now will be revealed, and there will be no power or helper. Use your strength now.

outline.heading: The returning rain and the splitting earth
outline.gist: Allah swears by the cycle of rain and growth that keeps life going; without rain, a desert. This is a decisive word.

outline.heading: No jest: the ultimate truth
outline.gist: The message is not exaggeration; forces we cannot imagine exist, yet each life is guarded for its term.

outline.heading: They plot and I plot
outline.gist: The disbelievers plan against the Prophet, and Allah has His own plan; we too try to succeed amid others' plans.

outline.heading: The first commands of Juz Amma
outline.gist: From An-Naba to here there are almost no commands, only concepts; At-Tariq ends with two.

outline.heading: Give them respite, gently
outline.gist: Convey the message and be patient; people respond on their own time, and you may fail with some, as the Prophet did with his uncles.

outline.heading: Element one: dependence on Allah in the heart
outline.gist: We control choices and effort, not outcomes; trusting Allah frees us from worrying about what we cannot change.

outline.heading: Element two: doing your job fully
outline.gist: Without exhausting your effort, tawakkul becomes wishful thinking; bring something worth having exposed.

outline.heading: The student who studied well still relies
outline.gist: Even with the curriculum mastered, infinite things can go wrong, so the prepared student still relies on Allah.

outline.heading: The crammer's arrogant hope
outline.gist: Expecting Allah to suspend the laws of the universe for a lazy student is arrogance and can erode faith.

outline.heading: The Prophet exhausted every effort
outline.gist: He struggled for Allah as Allah deserves and wasted no moment; tawakkul without effort is not practised.

outline.heading: Element three: being okay when it doesn't go your way
outline.gist: The Prophet grew impatient in mid-Mecca and was told to give them time. Accept the result, get up and try again, never objecting to Allah's decree.

outline.heading: The first tool in the kit
outline.gist: Living tawakkul is a key difference between Muslims and others: do your job and be content with the result.

LIITps_-hOo.title: Surah Summaries: Surat At-Takwir and Al-Infitar
LIITps_-hOo.one_line: At-Takwir presents human free will as a sacred gift from Allah; Al-Infitar says that gift comes with accountability.
LIITps_-hOo.summary: He opens the second group of the last juz, five surahs about freedom of choice. At-Takwir lists cosmic events of the Last Day that no one can choose or stop, then describes Jibreel, the most revered creature, who also has no choice, and answers the charge of madness, the one accusation that is not a choice. Against all this stands the closing verse: you only will because Allah willed you to have a will. He insists this verse affirms human choice rather than cancelling it; free will is taken directly from God and is sacred. In the middle sits the buried infant girl asked for what sin she was killed. He suggests the question is really aimed at those who chose, and links it to children buried under the rubble of their homes today. Al-Infitar adds the next element: the problem is not being deceived by Allah's generosity but refusing to believe in accountability, the root meaning of deen. He warns parents and communities against trying to control others' choices; their job is to inform, support and inspire. He asks the audience to treat every decision as exercising a holy right they will answer for.

outline.heading: Recap: the three pillars of faith
outline.gist: The first group gave Allah's narrative, the tool and obstacle, and the code of conduct, all without ritual detail.

outline.heading: The second group: five surahs on freedom of choice
outline.gist: Each of the next five surahs looks at human choice from a different angle.

outline.heading: Only the human being chooses
outline.gist: Animals live by instinct, like the clockwork of a salmon run; humans alone weigh options and ask why, and that ability is a sacred gift.

outline.heading: Events of the Last Day we cannot stop
outline.gist: The sun wrapped, stars dimmed, mountains moved, oceans set ablaze, scrolls spread, Hell kindled and Paradise brought near.

outline.heading: You have impact now; soon you won't
outline.gist: On that day we only observe and are moved; losing the ability to affect anything hurts. Every soul knows what it brought.

outline.heading: Oaths by the stars, the night and the breathing dawn
outline.gist: Allah swears by the receding stars, the departing night and the morning as it takes its first breath.

outline.heading: Jibreel the noble messenger; the Prophet is not mad
outline.gist: The word is from a mighty, trusted, obeyed messenger; the Prophet saw him on the clear horizon and withholds nothing of the unseen.

outline.heading: Jibreel has no choice; madness is not a choice
outline.gist: The highest creature does not choose to obey. Of all charges against the Prophet, Allah rebuts insanity, the one that would deny he conveys by choice.

outline.heading: So where are you going?
outline.gist: No one can run from these events; the Quran is a reminder for whoever wills to walk straight.

outline.heading: You only will because Allah willed you a will
outline.gist: The verse is often misread as denying choice. Allah decreed that humans have choice; we take it directly from Him, which is why other creatures marvel at human disobedience.

outline.heading: The buried girl asked for what sin she was killed
outline.gist: In the middle of the cosmic upheaval comes one question to the infant girl buried alive, who made no choice and committed no sin.

outline.heading: The question is for us: children under the rubble
outline.gist: Perhaps the question is for those who chose to kill or allowed it. Our generation has let far more children die under bombed homes than pre-Islamic Arabia ever buried.

outline.heading: No one can take your freedom of choice
outline.gist: Whatever your poverty or status, choice was granted by Allah; every decision exercises a holy right. Respect it.

outline.heading: Losing freedom wounds the soul
outline.gist: The worst punishment is taking away freedom, which is why prisons exist; it stabs the soul.

outline.heading: Why the final message came to free Arabs
outline.gist: The Arabs of the time answered to no one, so they understood what Allah was offering in free will.

outline.heading: What deceived you about your generous Lord?
outline.gist: The sky splits and graves are overturned; then the human being is asked what lured him away from the Lord who shaped and balanced him.

outline.heading: Deen means accountability
outline.gist: The real problem is denying the deen, whose root meaning is being held to account; later it names law and religion.

outline.heading: Nobody wants to be held accountable
outline.gist: At school and work we seek places with no accountability, yet every choice we ever made will be brought back.

outline.heading: A generation taught not to choose
outline.gist: He grew up being told to keep his head down and let parents choose everything. A father once walked his son out of his talk on freedom of choice.

outline.heading: Inspire and support, but do not control
outline.gist: Parents educate and aid; the child will answer for their own choices. Controlling those Allah allowed to choose is a dangerous thought. Every deed is recorded by noble scribes.

outline.heading: A day when no one controls anything
outline.gist: On that day all command belongs to Allah; choice is taken away and every choice is answered for.

72:1.ar: قُلۡ أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ أَنَّهُ ٱسۡتَمَعَ نَفَرࣱ مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ فَقَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا سَمِعۡنَا قُرۡءَانًا عَجَبࣰ ا
72:1.en: Say (O Muhammad): It is revealed unto me that a company of the Jinn gave ear, and they said: Lo! we have heard a marvellous Qur'an

72:2.ar: يَهۡدِيٓ إِلَى ٱلرُّشۡدِ فَـَٔامَنَّا بِهِۦۖ وَلَن نُّشۡرِكَ بِرَبِّنَآ أَحَدࣰ ا
72:2.en: Which guideth unto righteousness, so we believe in it and we ascribe no partner unto our Lord

72:3.ar: وَأَنَّهُۥ تَعَٰلَىٰ جَدُّ رَبِّنَا مَا ٱتَّخَذَ صَٰحِبَةࣰ وَلَا وَلَدࣰ ا
72:3.en: And (we believe) that He - exalted be the glory of our Lord! - hath taken neither wife nor son

72:4.ar: وَأَنَّهُۥ كَانَ يَقُولُ سَفِيهُنَا عَلَى ٱللَّهِ شَطَطࣰ ا
72:4.en: And that the foolish one among us used to speak concerning Allah an atrocious lie

72:5.ar: وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّآ أَن لَّن تَقُولَ ٱلۡإِنسُ وَٱلۡجِنُّ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبࣰ ا
72:5.en: And lo! we had supposed that humankind and jinn would not speak a lie concerning Allah

72:6.ar: وَأَنَّهُۥ كَانَ رِجَالࣱ مِّنَ ٱلۡإِنسِ يَعُوذُونَ بِرِجَالࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ فَزَادُوهُمۡ رَهَقࣰ ا
72:6.en: And indeed (O Muhammad) individuals of humankind used to invoke the protection of individuals of the jinn, so that they increased them in revolt against Allah

72:7.ar: وَأَنَّهُمۡ ظَنُّواْ كَمَا ظَنَنتُمۡ أَن لَّن يَبۡعَثَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدࣰ ا
72:7.en: And indeed they supposed, even as ye suppose, that Allah would not raise anyone (from the dead)

72:8.ar: وَأَنَّا لَمَسۡنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ فَوَجَدۡنَٰهَا مُلِئَتۡ حَرَسࣰ ا شَدِيدࣰ ا وَشُهُبࣰ ا
72:8.en: And (the Jinn who had listened to the Qur'an said): We had sought the heaven but had found it filled with strong warders and meteors

72:9.ar: وَأَنَّا كُنَّا نَقۡعُدُ مِنۡهَا مَقَٰعِدَ لِلسَّمۡعِۖ فَمَن يَسۡتَمِعِ ٱلۡأٓنَ يَجِدۡ لَهُۥ شِهَابࣰ ا رَّصَدࣰ ا
72:9.en: And we used to sit on places (high) therein to listen. But he who listeneth now findeth a flame in wait for him

72:10.ar: وَأَنَّا لَا نَدۡرِيٓ أَشَرٌّ أُرِيدَ بِمَن فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ أَمۡ أَرَادَ بِهِمۡ رَبُّهُمۡ رَشَدࣰ ا
72:10.en: And we know not whether harm is boded unto all who are in the earth, or whether their Lord intendeth guidance for them

72:11.ar: وَأَنَّا مِنَّا ٱلصَّٰلِحُونَ وَمِنَّا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَۖ كُنَّا طَرَآئِقَ قِدَدࣰ ا
72:11.en: And among us there are righteous folk and among us there are far from that. We are sects having different rules

72:12.ar: وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّآ أَن لَّن نُّعۡجِزَ ٱللَّهَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَن نُّعۡجِزَهُۥ هَرَبࣰ ا
72:12.en: And we know that we cannot escape from Allah in the earth, nor can we escape by flight

72:13.ar: وَأَنَّا لَمَّا سَمِعۡنَا ٱلۡهُدَىٰٓ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦۖ فَمَن يُؤۡمِنۢ بِرَبِّهِۦ فَلَا يَخَافُ بَخۡسࣰ ا وَلَا رَهَقࣰ ا
72:13.en: And when we heard the guidance, we believed therein, and whoso believeth in his Lord, he feareth neither loss nor oppression

72:14.ar: وَأَنَّا مِنَّا ٱلۡمُسۡلِمُونَ وَمِنَّا ٱلۡقَٰسِطُونَۖ فَمَنۡ أَسۡلَمَ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ تَحَرَّوۡاْ رَشَدࣰ ا
72:14.en: And there are among us some who have surrendered (to Allah) and there are among us some who are unjust. And whoso hath surrendered to Allah, such have taken the right path purposefully

72:15.ar: وَأَمَّا ٱلۡقَٰسِطُونَ فَكَانُواْ لِجَهَنَّمَ حَطَبࣰ ا
72:15.en: And as for those who are unjust, they are firewood for hell

72:16.ar: وَأَلَّوِ ٱسۡتَقَٰمُواْ عَلَى ٱلطَّرِيقَةِ لَأَسۡقَيۡنَٰهُم مَّآءً غَدَقࣰ ا
72:16.en: If they (the idolaters) tread the right path, We shall give them to drink of water in abundance

72:17.ar: لِّنَفۡتِنَهُمۡ فِيهِۚ وَمَن يُعۡرِضۡ عَن ذِكۡرِ رَبِّهِۦ يَسۡلُكۡهُ عَذَابࣰ ا صَعَدࣰ ا
72:17.en: That We may test them thereby, and whoso turneth away from the remembrance of his Lord; He will thrust him into ever-growing torment

72:18.ar: وَأَنَّ ٱلۡمَسَٰجِدَ لِلَّهِ فَلَا تَدۡعُواْ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ أَحَدࣰ ا
72:18.en: And the places of worship are only for Allah, so pray not unto anyone along with Allah

72:19.ar: وَأَنَّهُۥ لَمَّا قَامَ عَبۡدُ ٱللَّهِ يَدۡعُوهُ كَادُواْ يَكُونُونَ عَلَيۡهِ لِبَدࣰ ا
72:19.en: And when the slave of Allah stood up in prayer to Him, they crowded on him, almost stifling

72:20.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّمَآ أَدۡعُواْ رَبِّي وَلَآ أُشۡرِكُ بِهِۦٓ أَحَدࣰ ا
72:20.en: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): I pray unto Allah only, and ascribe unto Him no partner

72:21.ar: قُلۡ إِنِّي لَآ أَمۡلِكُ لَكُمۡ ضَرࣰّ ا وَلَا رَشَدࣰ ا
72:21.en: Say: Lo! I control not hurt nor benefit for you

72:22.ar: قُلۡ إِنِّي لَن يُجِيرَنِي مِنَ ٱللَّهِ أَحَدࣱ وَلَنۡ أَجِدَ مِن دُونِهِۦ مُلۡتَحَدًا
72:22.en: Say: Lo! none can protect me from Allah, nor can I find any refuge beside Him

72:23.ar: إِلَّا بَلَٰغࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِسَٰلَٰتِهِۦۚ وَمَن يَعۡصِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ فَإِنَّ لَهُۥ نَارَ جَهَنَّمَ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَبَدًا
72:23.en: (Mine is) but conveyance (of the Truth) from Allah, and His messages; and whoso disobeyeth Allah and His messenger, lo! his is fire of hell, wherein such dwell for ever

72:24.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا رَأَوۡاْ مَا يُوعَدُونَ فَسَيَعۡلَمُونَ مَنۡ أَضۡعَفُ نَاصِرࣰ ا وَأَقَلُّ عَدَدࣰ ا
72:24.en: Till (the day) when they shall behold that which they are promised (they may doubt); but then they will know (for certain) who is weaker in allies and less in multitude

72:25.ar: قُلۡ إِنۡ أَدۡرِيٓ أَقَرِيبࣱ مَّا تُوعَدُونَ أَمۡ يَجۡعَلُ لَهُۥ رَبِّيٓ أَمَدًا
72:25.en: Say (O Muhammad, unto the disbelievers): I know not whether that which ye are promised is nigh, or if my Lord hath set a distant term for it

72:26.ar: عَٰلِمُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ فَلَا يُظۡهِرُ عَلَىٰ غَيۡبِهِۦٓ أَحَدًا
72:26.en: (He is) the Knower of the Unseen, and He revealeth unto none His secret

72:27.ar: إِلَّا مَنِ ٱرۡتَضَىٰ مِن رَّسُولࣲ فَإِنَّهُۥ يَسۡلُكُ مِنۢ بَيۡنِ يَدَيۡهِ وَمِنۡ خَلۡفِهِۦ رَصَدࣰ ا
72:27.en: Save unto every messenger whom He hath chosen, and then He maketh a guard to go before him and a guard behind him

72:28.ar: لِّيَعۡلَمَ أَن قَدۡ أَبۡلَغُواْ رِسَٰلَٰتِ رَبِّهِمۡ وَأَحَاطَ بِمَا لَدَيۡهِمۡ وَأَحۡصَىٰ كُلَّ شَيۡءٍ عَدَدَۢا
72:28.en: That He may know that they have indeed conveyed the messages of their Lord. He surroundeth all their doings, and He keepeth count of all things

9:31.ar: ٱتَّخَذُوٓاْ أَحۡبَارَهُمۡ وَرُهۡبَٰنَهُمۡ أَرۡبَابࣰ ا مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡمَسِيحَ ٱبۡنَ مَرۡيَمَ وَمَآ أُمِرُوٓاْ إِلَّا لِيَعۡبُدُوٓاْ إِلَٰهࣰ ا وَٰحِدࣰ اۖ لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَۚ سُبۡحَٰنَهُۥ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ
9:31.en: They have taken as lords beside Allah their rabbis and their monks and the Messiah son of Mary, when they were bidden to worship only One Allah. There is no Allah save Him. Be He Glorified from all that they ascribe as partner (unto Him)
